header.running_head: The Manner in which Hadhrat Umar Faarooq (RA) Distributed Wealth

blocks.text: drew his sword, extended his wrist and said, 'If Rasulullaah ﷺ is dead, then Allaah is still alive and can never die (it is after all for Allaah that we are fighting).' He then fought until he was martyred. On the other hand, this person (Ubaydullaah the father of Uthmaan) was grazing goats at the time. Do you expect me to have the same regard for both persons?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) maintained this practice throughout his period of Khilaafah.[^1] The remainder of the narration will follow soon.[^2]
The Narration of Hadhrat Anas (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) and Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib both report that Hadhrat Umar (RA) stipulated five thousand for the Muhaajireen, four thousand for the Ansaar and also four thousand for the sons of the Muhaajireen who could not fight in the Battle of Badr. Amongst these were Hadhrat Umar (RA) the son of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Asad Makhzoomi (RA), Hadhrat Usaama (RA) the son of Hadhrat Zaid (RA), Hadhrat Muhammad (RA) the son of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash Asadi (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) the son of Hadhrat Umar (RA). To this, Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) said that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) (the son of Hadhrat Umar (RA)) did not belong to this group because of his virtues. He then enumerated the virtues (meaning that he should receive more than the others). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "Give it to me if I have a right to it, otherwise do not." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said to Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), "Include him amongst those who are to receive five thousand and record me amongst those who are to receive four thousand." "This is not at all what I meant," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) clarified. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "By Allaah! You and I cannot both be amongst those receiving five thousand."[^3]
The Narration of Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam in this Regard

Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was stipulating allowances, he stipulated two thousand Dirhams for Hadhrat Abdullaah, the son of Hadhrat Handhala (RA). When Hadhrat Talha (RA) brought his cousin along and Hadhrat Umar (RA) stipulated a lesser amount for him, Hadhrat Talha (RA) asked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! You have given more to that Ansaari than to my cousin (who is a Muhaajir)." "Yes," replied Hadhrat Umar (RA), "because I saw his father (Hadhrat Handhala (RA)) during the Battle of Uhud shielding himself with only his sword (he had no shield) and moving it like a camel (moves its tail in all directions.
